condition: Empty and intact with its screw cap and wrap-around label. Light scuffing on the body, no cracks or residue.

safety.handling_warning: Rinse with water and let it dry before cutting.

concepts.title: Self-watering herb planter
concepts.description: Cut the bottle in two and turn the top into a wicking pot that sits in its own water reservoir.
steps: Peel off the label and mark a line 12 cm up from the base.
Score the line with a craft knife, then finish the cut with scissors.
Heat a nail and push it through the centre of the cap to make a wick hole.
Thread a 20 cm length of cotton string through the cap, knotting it on the inside.
Turn the top half upside down into the base so the wick hangs into the reservoir.
Fill the top with potting mix, plant a tulsi or mint cutting and fill the base with water.
concepts.image_prompt: A clear 1-litre PET water bottle cut in half and turned into a self-watering planter with a mint plant growing in the top section, a cotton wick reaching into water in the base

concepts.title: Slow drip feeder for potted plants
concepts.description: Push the capped bottle into the soil so it releases water to the roots over a day or two.
steps: Remove the label and rinse the bottle.
Heat a nail and make three small holes in the cap.
Fill the bottle with water and screw the cap on tightly.
Push the bottle neck-down into the soil beside the plant until it stands on its own.
Refill when empty; widen the holes if it drains slower than every two days.
concepts.image_prompt: A clear PET water bottle pushed upside down into the soil of a terracotta pot as a slow drip feeder for a chilli plant

concepts.title: PET garden twine
concepts.description: Cut the body into one long continuous strip to make strong, weatherproof twine for tying up plants.
steps: Cut off the base cleanly so the body is an open cylinder.
Set the bottle cutter jig to a 5 mm strip width.
Start a strip at the cut edge and pull the bottle through the jig in one steady motion.
Stop where the shoulder begins to curve and trim the strip there.
Wind the strip around a piece of card to keep it flat.
Use it to tie tomato and bean plants to their stakes; it will not rot in the rain.
